Today's release of macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6 includes a brand new Golden Gate Bridge dynamic wallpaper, bringing the total number of dynamic wallpapers to five. All of the following can be downloaded.

The wallpaper collection for macOS 27 Golden Gate continues to expand

When Apple announced macOS 27 Golden Gate at WWDC26, all operating systems used the same system wallpaper featuring a stylized number 27.

However, after several developer versions, Apple began adding dynamic screensavers that can also be used as wallpapers, featuring beautiful slow-motion video overlooking San Francisco's iconic Golden Gate Bridge.

When the Mac is unlocked, the screensaver will slowly come to a stop, leaving behind a fresh yet slightly different wallpaper each time it pauses.

Although the dynamic effects are handled by macOS, you can find a gallery of still screenshots from the four videos below, along with light and dark versions of the generic stylized 27 wallpaper.

Remember to click on the image and save the full-resolution version. To set it as your background, go to 'System Settings' > 'Wallpaper', scroll down to 'Your Photos', click the 'Add Photo' button, then do any of the following:

Add a photo from your Photos library: click 'Choose from Photos', then select a photo. Add an image file: click 'Choose File', select a file, then click 'Open'. You can also drag an image from your desktop or a folder onto the thumbnail at the top of the Wallpaper settings. Add a folder from Finder: click 'Choose Folder', select a folder, then click 'Open'. Add an album or folder from the Photos app: select an album or folder under 'Photo Collections'.

According to Apple, 'You can also choose a custom wallpaper without opening Wallpaper settings':

Use a photo from your Photos library: go to the Photos app, select a photo, click the share button in the Photos toolbar, then click 'Set as Wallpaper'. Use an image you found online: Control-click the image in a Safari window, then select 'Use Image as Desktop Wallpaper'. Use an image saved on your Mac: click the Finder icon in the Dock to open a Finder window. Control-click the image file, then click 'Set as Desktop Picture'.

To learn more about how to set custom wallpapers in macOS, please click this link.
